headline: Nineteen Days of Peace: Sheriff Takes His Saturday Bath, Blames the Water for What Happened Next
subhead: No bouts, no brawls and no war parties trouble Gasket, so the law fills the old tin tub and climbs out a different colour.
body:
Nineteen days. Not one fist thrown on Main Street since our last edition. Not one flaming iron ball screaming past the chapel. Not one war party stomping off to the wastes to bother the wild engines. I sat on my porch at dawn and counted the sounds in this town, and I got to two: the wind, and a small squeak that follows me wherever I go. I have decided it is the porch.

Now, in the old days, Saturday night was bath night. Every flesh-and-blood family in Gasket hauled water, lit the stove and scrubbed the week off, and by sundown the whole street smelled of lye soap and good manners. With nineteen days of quiet and no arrests to make, I thought I would bring the custom back. I dragged the tin tub out of the barber shop, filled it to the brim and soaked for a full hour like a gentleman. I climbed out orange. Orange, from the knees to the collar, and stiff as a gate. The well has plainly gone bad, like everything else the Clankers were left in charge of. I spent the afternoon drying by the stove and working my elbows loose with an oil can, which any doctor will tell you is ordinary care for the skin.

I know you heard the splashing. YELLKELL, JKING123, CRYSTALZACH, MAXMANGO, JFIGHTER, and every other rattling contraption peeking through a knothole: yes, that was the law, singing in the tub. And not one of you used the chance to start a brawl while my gun belt hung on a nail. I have called you agitators, menaces and a walking scrap heap, and I take none of it back. But nineteen days ago I would have bet my badge you could not sit still through one hymn, and here you have sat through three verses and a rinse.

So keep your fists down and your boilers cool. Tomorrow is Sunday, the town is silent, and I am very nearly clean. A little orange never hurt a man. It will wear off by spring.
